significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that “the velocity and direction of this drift across turns” predict later jailbreak compliance with several turns of lead time, while a “restoring force” causally suppresses that outcome without sacrificing benign utility—a form-(iii) predictive coupling combined with a form-(ii) intervention. This fixes expectations for unseen attack trajectories and distinguishes malicious from benign topic drift; Crescendo (Russinovich et al., USENIX Security 2025) makes the specific question consequential by showing that gradual multi-turn escalation can bypass refusals. The phenomenon and mechanism are both determinate, and a negative result would rule out one-dimensional drift velocity as an early-warning signal and the anchored geometry as a sufficient causal defense, rather than merely reporting non-detection. In the topic-substitution check, deleting the velocity-to-future-compliance relation and restoring-force mechanism leaves only generic mechanistic LLM safety, which would not earn this score.

reach.justification: The named handles are “drift velocity” as an online predictor and the per-turn “restoring-force intervention”; the former is explicitly ex ante because it forecasts compliance “several turns before” it occurs, leaving time to gate or modify generation. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction—drift velocity forecasts later compliance across attacks—remains a relation to test rather than merely a procedure for rediscovering an arbitrary direction, although the first-turn anchor and white-box access constrain deployment. The asserted “attack-agnostic” scope supports use by model auditors and operators across multi-turn attacks, while the intervention offers an actionable shipping-time monitor and control rather than only post-hoc explanation. Topic substitution removes both the turns-ahead predictor and intervention, leaving no comparable handle or lead time, so the score comes from the claim rather than from the general importance of LLM safety.
